claims.claim: The OECD–Eurostat Entrepreneurship Indicators Programme defines entrepreneurship as the phenomenon associated with entrepreneurial activity: enterprising human action in pursuit of generating value through creation or expansion of economic activity by identifying and exploiting new products, processes, or markets.

In the OECD–Eurostat framework, an entrepreneur is a business owner seeking value through creation or expansion, entrepreneurial activity is the action, and entrepreneurship is the phenomenon associated with that action.
The OECD–Eurostat framework recognizes entrepreneurial activity within firms by people without ownership stakes; entrepreneurship is not exclusive to small businesses or self-employment.

The OECD states that not all new businesses are necessarily entrepreneurial and that large companies can be entrepreneurial; the 2021 Outlook likewise says entrepreneurship is not synonymous with SMEs or startups.
OpenStax presents entrepreneurial ventures as activities that include risk in acting on opportunities not previously established and says such ventures can be for-profit or nonprofit.
OpenStax characterizes calculated risk as action after due diligence—research and investigation intended to make informed decisions and minimize risk—and distinguishes it from certainty.
OpenStax describes intrapreneurs as employees who apply creativity, vision, and risk-taking inside larger organizations, while the employer provides salary and financial backing.

OpenStax sources acknowledge both that a small-business owner may be an entrepreneur and that course definitions sometimes distinguish entrepreneurial innovation from operating an established small-business model.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether entrepreneurs and small-business owners should be treated as separate categories.
positions: OpenStax Entrepreneurship says small-business owners and franchisees may be entrepreneurs when they introduce something new to a region or market.
OpenStax Introduction to Business 2e distinguishes entrepreneurship from small-business management and describes owners who operate established models as a different case.
OECD treats entrepreneurship as value-creating activity rather than a firm-size or ownership category.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents overlap rather than a rigid binary. It directs readers to state the definition being applied and assesses the action—creation, expansion, or novelty under uncertainty—rather than assigning status from company size alone.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft supplied no substantive definition, evidence, or source-backed distinctions.
The generated draft's topic vocabulary was circular and did not distinguish person, activity, and phenomenon.
The generated draft implied generic application without explaining uncertainty, ownership, or the limits of the small-business comparison.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate with a definition based on the OECD–Eurostat entrepreneurship measurement framework.
Added distinctions among entrepreneur, entrepreneurial activity, and entrepreneurship.
Qualified the relationship between entrepreneurship and small-business ownership rather than treating either term as universally inclusive or exclusive.
Added a worked example of entrepreneurial action by an employee, without teaching idea-generation or problem-validation methods.
Removed any implication that entrepreneurship guarantees profit, growth, or success.

sourceRecords.title: Entrepreneurship at a Glance 2011
sourceRecords.provider: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sourceRecords.notes: Official OECD PDF read directly. Supports the EIP definitions on pages 3–4 and 15–16: entrepreneur, entrepreneurial activity, and entrepreneurship; activity inside firms without an ownership stake; entrepreneurship not limited to small firms or self-employment; not every new firm is necessarily entrepreneurial; and failure does not remove the entrepreneurial character of an attempted activity. No reuse license was verified, so this source is used for factual reference only.

sourceRecords.title: OECD SME and Entrepreneurship Outlook 2021
sourceRecords.provider: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sourceRecords.notes: Official OECD PDF read directly, especially page 114. Supports the current OECD restatement that entrepreneurship is not synonymous with SMEs or startups and concerns value-seeking activity through creation, expansion, or identifying and exploiting new products, processes, or markets. No reuse license was verified; facts only.

sourceRecords.notes: Page read live.
